2610.06985.title: CrystalJev: thinking fast and slow with atomistic foundation models for materials discovery
2610.06985.paper_summary: Atomistic foundation models triage millions of hypothetical materials but are used as slow simulators, their thresholded energies taken at face value. They are better read as fast decision-makers. CrystalJev queries a frozen interatomic potential once per unrelaxed structure and answers typed questions with calibrated probabilities, finite-sample guarantees and a rule for when to think slowly. Across 65 Matbench Discovery models, a 'stable' call is a probability in disguise, explained by a model's errors and the candidate population. Once trained, one forward pass decides nearly as well as a relaxation at a thirtieth of its cost, and a value-of-information theory sends slower computation only where decisions can change. The same layer answers electronic, mechanical and molecular questions. In a registered prospective test with 700 new density-functional calculations, single-pass forecasts calibrated only on existing data over-stated the stable fraction of unseen candidates (5.8%) by at most 2.1 percentage points.
2610.06985.paper_summary_zh: 原子基礎模型篩選數百萬種假設材料，但作為緩慢的模擬器使用，其閾值能量被視為表面價值。它們更應被視為快速決策者。CrystalJev 每次對未放鬆的結構查詢一次凍結的原子間勢，並以經過校準的概率、有限樣本保證以及何時慢思考的規則回答輸入的問題。在 65 個 Matbench Discovery 模型中，'穩定'的呼叫實際上是一種偽裝的概率，由模型的誤差和候選人群體解釋。一旦訓練完成，一次前向傳遞的決策幾乎能與以三十分之一成本的放鬆效果相當，而信息價值理論則僅在決策可能改變的地方發送較慢的計算。同一層回答電子、機械和分子問題。在一項註冊的前瞻性測試中，使用 700 個新的密度泛函計算，僅基於現有數據的單次預測將未見候選者的穩定比例（5.8%）高估了最多 2.1 個百分點。
